check_response.question: Is the person responding? Tap their shoulder and shout their name.
check_response.voice: Is the person responding? Tap their shoulder and shout their name.

check_breathing.question: Look at the chest for up to 10 seconds. Is the person breathing normally?
check_breathing.voice: Look at the chest for up to ten seconds. Is the person breathing normally?

act_cpr.voice: Start CPR now. Push hard and fast in time with the beat.

action.title: Start CPR
steps: Shout for help. Ask a crewmate to bring the defibrillator (AED) and the medical kit and to contact the flight surgeon.
Secure the person and yourself to a fixed surface or restraint, so you can push without drifting away. In microgravity, CPR positions differ from Earth: use the method from your crew training.
Place the heel of one hand on the centre of the chest and the other hand on top. Keep your arms straight.
Push hard and fast in time with the metronome: 100 to 120 pushes per minute, about 5 cm (2 in) deep. Let the chest rise fully between pushes.
If you are trained, give 2 rescue breaths after every 30 pushes. If not, keep pushing without stopping.
When the defibrillator arrives, switch it on and follow its voice instructions.
Do not stop until the person moves or breathes normally, the defibrillator tells you to stop, or another crew member takes over.

act_recovery.voice: The person is breathing but not responding. Keep the airway open and watch them closely.

action.title: Unresponsive but breathing
steps: Secure the person so they cannot drift or hit equipment.
Keep the head tilted slightly back so the airway stays open. Clear anything visible from the mouth.
Ask a crewmate to contact the flight surgeon now and to bring the medical kit.
Check breathing again every minute. If breathing stops or becomes gasping, press Back, answer No, and start CPR.
Do not give food, drink or medicine.

options.label: Confusion, weakness, drooping face or slurred speech

chest_symptoms.question: Is the chest pain together with sweating, nausea, pain in the arm or jaw, or shortness of breath?
chest_symptoms.voice: Is the chest pain together with sweating, nausea, pain in the arm or jaw, or shortness of breath?

act_cardiac.voice: This may be a heart emergency. Keep the person still and contact the flight surgeon now.

action.title: Possible heart emergency
steps: Stop all activity. Keep the person calm and still, and secure them so they do not drift.
Ask a crewmate to bring the defibrillator and the medical kit and to contact the flight surgeon immediately.
Ask the flight surgeon whether to give aspirin. Do not give it if the person is allergic or has been told not to take it.
Measure pulse, blood pressure and SpO2 and tell the flight surgeon the numbers.
If the person stops responding, press Restart. The guide will lead you to CPR.

act_chest_watch.voice: Rest and measure vital signs. Tell the flight surgeon even if the pain goes away.

action.title: Chest pain without other warning signs
steps: Rest and stay with the person.
Measure pulse, blood pressure and SpO2 (open Measure after you end this guide).
Tell the flight surgeon about the pain, even if it goes away.
If new symptoms appear (sweating, nausea, arm or jaw pain, shortness of breath), press Restart and answer again.

act_breathing.voice: Help the person stay calm. Check the cabin air alarms and measure oxygen.

action.title: Difficulty breathing
steps: Help the person stay calm and take slow breaths. Keep them secured in a comfortable position.
Check the cabin alarms for oxygen and CO2 and check that ventilation works.
Measure SpO2 and tell the flight surgeon the value.
Contact the flight surgeon immediately and ask about supplemental oxygen.
If the lips look blue, or the person cannot speak a full sentence, treat it as life-threatening and call all crew for help.

act_neuro.voice: These can be signs of a stroke. Note the time and contact the flight surgeon immediately.

action.title: Possible stroke or brain problem
steps: Note the time when the symptoms started and tell the flight surgeon.
Keep the person still and secured. Do not give food, drink or medicine.
Measure blood glucose if a meter is available, because low glucose can look similar.
Contact the flight surgeon immediately.

act_general.voice: Stay with the person, measure vital signs and contact the flight surgeon.

action.title: General check
steps: Stay with the person and keep them comfortable and secured.
Measure pulse, blood pressure, temperature and SpO2 (open Measure after you end this guide).
Contact the flight surgeon and describe what you see.
If the person gets worse, press Restart and answer again.
